newsitem.title: UK: London gold feels aftershocks of Swiss sales news.
newsitem.headline: London gold feels aftershocks of Swiss sales news.

text.p: The gold market hovered at depressed levels on Thursday as it digested news that Switzerland planned to liquidate some bullion holdings.

Gold fixed $2.35 lower at $352.15 per ounce the morning after Switzerland's president proposed a transfer of revalued bullion reserves to a foundation to assist victims of the Holocaust and other tragedies.
Volume was lacklustre in Europe, with traders pegging support at $351, but analysts said the market was likely to test the psychological $350 level once the New York market opens.
So far on Thursday spot gold bids have held to a narrow range of $353.20-$351.40 after touching $350.65 on Wednesday.

Prices had already slipped from a peak of $364 two days before the news from Switzerland hit the market and some analysts thought gold may be settling back into a downtrend that saw it fix at a 3-3/4 year low of 336.90 on February 12.

The estimated 40 tonnes of gold to be sold by the Swiss humanitarian foundation over 10 years could be absorbed by the market, but the announcement raised the spectre of other central banks liquidating bullion.

"I know the people from the central bank and they should be able to do it without affecting the market, that's why I am not worried about the actual sale," said analyst Hanspeter Hausheer of Swiss Bank Corp.
"It's the psychological affect...one central bank doesn't do something like this without discussing it with other banks," he added.
Analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland said prices were unlikely to soon recover from the shock.
"The gold price was $357 on the announcement by the Swiss National Bank; remember it well, it may be a long time coming round again," he said.
There also could be moves by the SNB to scrap restrictions on gold swaps and remove a requirement of a 40 percent gold backing to bank notes, he added.
The Swiss move may give impetus to use gold to finance other good causes. "Who's next? What cause is next," Smith asked.
Silver was more resilient, indicated one cent firmer at $5.18/$5.20 per ounce and attempting to stabilise, analysts said.
Solid support was pegged at $5.15, they added.
Platinum had been hit by professional selling in the morning, indicated $3.00 weaker at $378.00/$379.00 per ounce, continuing its fall from $406 touched on February 28.
A firm floor was seen at $375, dealers said.
Palladium had already hit bottom at $142.25 on Wednesday and was quoted $2.50 firmer at $145.00/$146.00 per ounce.
